findings.summary: Three other places still say admission scans the files a request names; the plan's grep missed them.
findings.evidence: I grepped for '(file|files) (it|the request) names'. docs/enforcement.md row M19 says `athena ask` runs the scan 'on the request and the files it names before admitting a job'. The doc comment on `boundary_scan` in briefs.rs says 'Athena runs it on a request and on the files the request names'. The comment in `the_admission_scan_finds_what_the_policy_scan_finds` in xtask/tests/policy.rs says 'Athena scans a request and the files it names'. After the change, all three will be wrong. Fix: Reword these three comments and the doc row to say admission scans only the request's own text. They are comment and doc edits only: no code changes, and `boundary_scan` and the word lists stay as they are, so they fit the scope. If editing athena-context or xtask is judged out of scope, say so in the change description.
findings.location: Plan, Open questions 2 / Files list; docs/enforcement.md:33, crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs:622-623, xtask/tests/policy.rs:235

findings.summary: admission.rs is a listed deliverable, but the plan leaves it unchanged. The reason is sound and should go in the change description.
findings.evidence: The reading already notes that admission.rs holds no boundary scan, and the plan's grep agrees. The deliverables list still says 'crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs (modify)'. Fix: Keep the decision. Have the producer state in its summary that the scan lives in reading.rs (`scan_request_input`), so admission.rs needs no change.

summary: I read the code the plan names and it matches. `scan_request_input` is at reading.rs:2030, and its named-file loop is at 2043-2060. `refuse_banned_input` is at 2066, and its only callers are `ask` (715) and `queue` (740). The only outside caller is the run/mod.rs:2466 test. `request_text_touches` has other callers (steward, hestia, code_health) and stays. The fixtures `repo`, `athena` and `commit_file` exist in run/mod.rs, and the existing tests already use the `["sand","box"].concat()` trick. The plan fixes the fault where it starts: it removes the named-file loop and the git parameters that only that loop needed, rather than exempting BRIEF.md. That is the general fix, not a special case. The criterion-1 demonstration calls the real `ask` entry point with a named file holding a boundary word, and it would fail under the old loop. The criterion-2 demonstration checks that a boundary word in the request's own text is still refused, through both `ask` and `queue`, with source `request`. The changelog plan does not rewrite history. The work fits one producer run. The only gaps are three stale descriptions of the old behavior (docs/enforcement.md M19, the briefs.rs doc comment, the xtask policy test comment) and the unchanged admission.rs deliverable. Both are minor or nit, so I accept the plan.
